stories.title: Cellular Provider InfiniG Secures $5M Seed Funding
stories.excerpt: InfiniG, an enterprise cellular platform for commercial real estate, announced Tuesday that it has raised a $5.2 million seed round. Early-stage venture capital firms J2 Ventures and Stormbreaker Ventures led the round. Los Gatos, Calif.-based InfiniG said it will use the funding to expand its mobile coverage as a service (MCaaS) product rollouts, automate mobile-operator integration, scale its InfiniG Insights, and advance the platform’s automation and physical artificial intelligence. InfiniG’s MCaaS platform enables building owners to deploy neutral-host, multicarrier indoor cellular coverage without the complexity and cost of traditional distributed antenna systems, according to the company. The platform also creates an upgradeable foundation for future 5G services, private wireless networks, physical AI and connected-building applications. “The mobile operators — the AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobiles of the world — have traditionally provided coverage,” said Joel Lindholm, co-founder and CEO at InfiniG. “The processes that have been used for the last 10 to 20 years really require people to come into each building using those processes and their own technologies, and that’s been very limiting. That’s why only the biggest buildings or biggest venues have coverage. That’s also why you see most buildings in the United States do not have coverage, whether they be hospitals or hotels, offices, warehouses or manufacturing floors.” Lindholm’s firm stepped into the gap. “Our solution is focused on being able to cover those thousands of buildings instead of the hundreds of buildings from the legacy model. Fundamentally, we have to look at the world in a new way for the next decade. The 10- to 20-year-old technologies are just no longer satisfactory.” InfiniG uses Citizens Broadband Radio Service (CBRS), a non-carrier spectrum, to provide a single radio infrastructure in a building that is shared equally across all the mobile operators. The platform eliminates traditional distributed antenna system (DAS) friction and enables multicarrier coverage via software-driven automation. InfiniG plans to expand rollouts, automate carrier onboarding, and advance physical AI capabilities.

stories.title: Benderson Picks Up 3 Florida Retail Assets for Nearly $37M
stories.excerpt: Benderson Development acquired three retail properties on the Gulf Coast, totaling 400,000 square feet. The company paid $36.91 million for the three properties. The first acquisition is Granada Plaza, a Publix-anchored retail center located in the Tampa suburb of Dunedin at the intersection of Main Street and Keene Road. The second acquisition is Venice Market Place, a shopping center at the intersection of Tamiami Trail and Center Road in Venice. It sold for nearly $10 million last month. Selig Enterprises was the seller. Benderson also purchased a retail building leased to Lowe’s Home Improvement at 10070 Estero Town Commons Place in Estero. Benderson bought the store for $9.5 million in June. It last sold in 2005 for $4.38 million. The property is located at 10070 Estero Town Commons Place Benderson is based in University Park and has more than 1,000 properties totaling 58 million square feet of retail space in its national portfolio. stories.summary: Benderson Development, a Sarasota-based retailer with 58M SF nationally, bought three Florida Gulf Coast retail properties totaling 400K SF for $36.91M. Assets include Granada Plaza (Publix anchor, Dunedin), Venice Market Place ($10M), and an Estero Lowe's box ($9.5M, resale of $4.38M 2005 purchase). Portfolio consolidation suggests ongoing landlord confidence in essential-anchored retail in Tampa Bay and Southwest Florida submarkets.
stories.impact: Moderate relevance to multifamily: Benderson's acquisition signal in Tampa Bay (Dunedin, Estero) reflects continued retail fundamentals and foot traffic in these high-growth submarkets. Strong retail anchors near multifamily sites can drive mixed-use development feasibility and co-tenancy quality. Monitor Tampa Bay rent growth and population influx—retail stabilization supports residential upside.

stories.title: Baptist Health Acquires 493K-SF Jax Medical Office Complex
stories.excerpt: Baptist Health paid $65 million for the Southbank Medical Pavilion, a 493,000-square-foot healthcare asset at 841 Prudential Drive in downtown Jacksonville. ShareMD was the seller. Transwestern represented ShareMD in the disposition to Baptist Health. The 22-story Southbank Medical Pavilion is 94% leased and situated on 7.9 acres along the Southbank of the St. Johns River. The property is directly adjacent to Baptist Health’s flagship campus and near Wolfson Children’s Hospital, Baptist MD Anderson Cancer Center and Nemours Children’s Health.  In addition to the medical tower, the property includes a six-story, 1,124-space parking garage totaling 324,212 square feet and two development outparcels. Transwestern’s Healthcare Capital Markets team of Steve Leathers, Bill Boyd, Seth Gilford, Jake Jordan, Angela Heidman, and Max Hastings represented ShareMD. The Transwestern Group led the marketing and sale process, generating offers from healthcare-focused investors, Jacksonville office investors and healthcare providers. stories.title: Samantha Atlas of Ash Staging: 5 Questions
stories.excerpt: Staging can play a critical role in residential real estate. It helps to bring a model unit to life, and it provides potential renters and buyers with a glimpse of what their future home could look like. Successfully staging requires more than a properly positioned couch and some art on the walls. Enter Ash Staging, a luxury staging and model residence design business that has completed thousands of projects — including commercial and hospitality spaces — over the last 15 years, representing over $50 billion in real estate. Samantha Atlas, senior director of projects at Ash Staging, has been with the firm for nine years. She splits her time between Los Angeles and New York City, and helped to launch the company’s West Coast office. Commercial Observer caught up with Atlas in mid-August to discuss her time with Ash Staging and the value of her work in real estate. This interview has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: What is the mission of Ash Staging? Samantha Atlas: I’ve been with Ash for a little over nine years now, and really seen it grow. I run the L.A. office, and I joined the company at a time of growth. Since I joined, the story has been, “How do we continue to grow and change the narrative of what staging can be?” Generally speaking, for a long time the idea around staging has been neutrality — nothing with a serious point of view. I came to work at Ash because we sort of eschewed that. We want to imbue personality. We want our clients and our potential buyers of these homes to have an emotional response — it’s what drives us. We believe in the power of paint and will really push our clients to invest outside of the staging into the property to get it sold. What we really believe in, and how we position ourselves as a brand, is being a partner alongside our real estate agents, clients and developers. What are some of the projects that Ash has staged? stories.title: Proptech Seed Rounds This Year Are in Full Bloom
stories.excerpt: To the surprise of some, or perhaps many, proptech has reportedly drawn the largest number of $5 million to $10 million seed rounds across industries in 2026. To the surprise of no one, artificial intelligence has a lot to do with those seed rounds. According to a Crunchbase report published July 31, at the top of the scale with $10 million seed rounds are proptech companies such as Breezy, a Los Angeles-based startup offering an AI operating system for residential real estate professionals; Grotto AI, a Manhattan-based IT and Internet firm offering AI-based tools for leasing and renewals; and Hint, a Charlotte, N.C.-based AI‑powered home‑management platform for homeowners. There have been at least 15 proptech seed rounds in the $5 million to $10 million scale so far in 2026, according to Crunchbase, which did not provide an overall number of deals in the category. A Center for Real Estate Technology and Innovation (CRETI) report found 30 deals in the $5 million to $10 million range in the first half of 2026 totaling $207.3 million and representing 4.6 percent of funding across all rounds. Overall proptech venture funding reached $4.53 billion across 231 disclosed funding rounds in the first half of 2026, with a median funding round of $6.75 million. Compared with the prior year, the market was broadly stable. First-half 2026 funding was down 0.6 percent from the first half of 2025 and up 2.6 percent from the first half of 2024, CRETI reported. The total number of seed fundings industry-by-industry is an elusive number. However, according to Seedtable, a global intelligence platform for startups, a typical seed round across industries is $2 million (median), stepping up to $9 million at Series A and $20 million at Series B. Seed is the most common stage by deal count, accounting for 29,708 tracked rounds in 2026. 100 CEO Caren Maio. This signals market belief in efficiency gains for leasing, resident engagement, and operations. Developers should audit current tech stack—underinvestment in leasing automation, tenant experience, and asset management software may become competitive liability as best-in-class competitors adopt AI-powered tools. Consider acquisition or partnership risks from well-funded proptech entrants.

stories.title: How Landlords Are Cutting Their Eviction Costs
stories.excerpt: By Tom DeRose, co-founder and CEO at PandaGuarantee ___________________________________________________________________________________________ Contested evictions in New York City are the most expensive in the world, running $15,000 to $50,000 each. But the single largest piece of that cost is missed rent, and missed rent is preventable. I started PandaGuarantee because the existing guarantor services were either too slow, too expensive or too confusing to applicants. The customer experience, both of the property owner and their tenants, seemed to be an afterthought. The thesis is simple: The rent guarantee process needs to be as efficient and affordable as possible. Applicant approvals in minutes, economical prices, and an easy to use platform that ties it all together. The $21,000 Problem When landlords think about evictions, they think about lawyers’ fees and court filings. That’s real money, but not where most of the damage is. The majority of the cost is rent — the opportunity cost of having an empty apartment or a squatter not paying for months. In a New York nonpayment proceeding, a landlord can easily go six months (or longer) without collecting while the case sits on the court’s docket. At $3,500 a month — roughly the median for a Manhattan one-bedroom — that’s $21,000 in lost income before you’ve paid a single attorney. Cover the missed rent, and you’ve cut the financial damage roughly in half. That’s the math behind rent guarantee insurance, and it’s why I started PandaGuarantee as a fast, easy, economical option for property owners to protect themselves from tenant default. 2019 Changed the Math Before the Housing Stability and Tenant Protection Act (HSTPA), landlords could ask borderline approvable applicants for larger security deposits. bullets: NYC contested evictions cost $15K–$50K; missed rent is largest cost component
PandaGuarantee founder: six-month+ rent loss (non-payment) exceeds legal/court fees
Rent guarantee platform automates applicant approvals, lowers operational friction, prevents vacancy
stories.summary: PandaGuarantee, founded by Tom DeRose, addresses the economic burden of evictions in NYC, where contested cases cost $15K–$50K each. The largest cost driver is missed rent during multi-month non-payment proceedings—not attorney fees. stories.title: Tavaco Properties Buys DMV Office for $29M
stories.excerpt: Tavaco Properties has added another discounted office property to its growing Greater Washington portfolio. The Los Angeles-based firm paid $28.5 million for a 272,300-square-foot building in Falls Church, Va., Business Journals first reported. Hawaii-based James Campbell Company sold the 14-story property at 3110 Fairview Park Drive after acquiring it for $43.7 million in 2016. Tavaco specializes in acquiring and optimizing underperforming assets, and the deal is its third D.C.-area office acquisition since late last year, totaling nearly $65 million. In March, a Tavaco affiliate paid $8.2 million for the 100,900-square-foot Twinbrook Plaza in Rockville, Md., which is about half the $15.5 million that an MRP Realty affiliate paid in 2016. Tavaco also acquired the eight-story, 275,480-square-foot Ballston Station in Arlington for $28 million in late 2025. The State Teachers Retirement System of Ohio had acquired that property for $58.2 million about 30 years ago. “We view Fairview, Ballston Station and Twinbrook Plaza as long-term additions to Tavaco’s portfolio,” Managing Director Sam Tavakoli told the Business Journals in a statement. He also added that the firm expects continued return-to-office trends to support demand for well-operated buildings. Indeed, U.S. office visits rose 6 percent in the first half of the year, although on-site attendance remained 31 percent below 2019 levels. James Campbell Company, meanwhile, has been reducing its national office exposure and concentrating more heavily on industrial assets. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.

stories.summary: Tavaco Properties, an LA-based opportunistic investor, paid $28.5M for a 272.3K-SF, 14-story office building in Falls Church, Va., representing a 35% discount from James Campbell Company's 2016 purchase price of $43.7M. This is Tavaco's third D.C.-area office acquisition in 12 months, totaling ~$65M, including Rockville's Twinbrook Plaza ($8.2M, down 47% from 2016) and Arlington's Ballston Station ($28M, down 52% from 30-year-old value).
stories.impact: DMV office-to-residential conversion opportunity signal: chronic DMV office underperformance (50%+ price declines over 5–8 years) creates conditions for value-add conversions to multifamily. Tavaco's repeated acquisition suggests it sees conversion arbitrage potential. However, check Falls Church zoning and entitlements—conversion feasibility and market demand for new units will determine whether this signals emerging supply opportunity or simply capital seeking yield in stabilized office. Monitor DMV office cap-rate compression and conversion costs.

stories.title: Taconic, NREA Add Premium Indian Restaurant to Hell’s Kitchen Mixed-Use
stories.excerpt: Taconic Partners and National Real Estate Advisors have signed a lease with Samudhra at The Ellery, a luxury mixed-use residential development at 312 W. 43rd St. in Hell’s Kitchen. The addition of the New Jersey-based premium Indian restaurant and lounge brings a new full-service dining destination to The Ellery. Samudhra will occupy approximately 10,000 square feet along West 43rd Street. The space will include a dedicated dining area, bar and lounge. The new location will mark Samudhra’s first outpost in New York City and second location overall. “Samudhra brings a premium new dining and social experience that will serve both our residents and the broader neighborhood,” George Tsapelas, SVP with Taconic Partners “From the outset, our vision for The Ellery has been to create a dynamic mixed-use destination that contributes to the energy of the area, and Samudhra further strengthens the retail and dining mix we’ve curated at the property.” Taconic and NREA were represented by Lon Rubackin, Michael Kadosh and Bevan Cohen from CBRE. Samudhra was represented by Brad Schwarz from Lee & Associates. The post Taconic, NREA Add Premium Indian Restaurant to Hell’s Kitchen Mixed-Use appeared first on Connect CRE.

This marks Samudhra's first NYC location and second overall. The space includes full dining, bar, and lounge, positioned to serve residents and the broader neighborhood.
stories.impact: Moderate; primarily indicates successful mixed-use retail/dining leasing at high-barrier Hell's Kitchen. The Ellery's ability to attract a premium, non-chain restaurant operator signals strong residential demand in the area and validates Taconic's mixed-use programming strategy. For developers: premium first-location restaurant commitments at lease-up demonstrate traffic confidence and brand aspiration—useful comp for underwriting retail NOI in Manhattan mixed-use projects. Monitor Hell's Kitchen rent growth and renter demographics for multifamily fundamentals.

stories.title: Landmark Properties Delivers 1,261-Bed Student Housing Near USC Campus
stories.excerpt: Landmark Properties has delivered The Standard at Los Angeles, a 429-unit, 1,261-bed student housing community at 3900 South Figueroa St., 0.3 miles from the University of Southern California in Los Angeles. It represents Landmark’s second ground-up development in LA. Rising eight stories, the project was designed by HED, with Landmark Construction, the in-house construction arm of Landmark Properties, serving as general contractor. “We’re excited to open doors at The Standard at Los Angeles and welcome our first residents to our community – just steps from USC’s campus, BMO Stadium and Memorial Coliseum,” said Jason Doornbos, chief development officer at Landmark Properties. “The Standard’s market-leading amenities, design, and luxury unit finishes set a new benchmark for student housing near USC, and this delivery reflects the caliber our team consistently delivers at Landmark.” In 2025, Landmark delivered its first development in the area, The Mark Los Angeles near UCLA, and also acquired Icon Plaza and West 27th Place, which serve students attending USC. For developers: university adjacency and lifestyle amenities continue to command premium rents and strong absorption in LA. Monitor USC/Figueroa corridor for additional multifamily and mixed-use competition and rent bifurcation by proximity to campus.
